output.name: Kiskan

anatomy.part: head, the eye of the gull
breast, the warm centre of the body
left wing shoulder, where the wing leaves the body

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up faster than any gull could follow. Kiskan was the first to try. She had a torn wing from a fight with a goat, and she flew until her chest burned and her feathers went salt-white. Tavo came up behind her, laughing, and took the wind out from under her. She dropped toward the sea, but the Gulls caught her in their hands and carried her up again, and she never got higher than the Windward. Ennu saw her and wove her shape into a kite so she could still be flown from the cliffs. Hesk keeps count of her. Her warm breast hangs in the north, bright and low, and when a boat comes home in fog the old women point to it. There she is, they say, still trying. Mend your net and wait for her.
output.verse:
Warm breast in the north,
Kiskan keeps her wings out wide,
she waits for the wind.
